title: Selector v2: add GPU/model/prompt benchmark matrix + v1/v2 comparison exporter
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Summary: This PR expands benchmark-lab to run Kernel Selector v2 experiments across a standardized GPU/model/prompt matrix and exports an explicit v1 vs v2 comparison table (CSV + Markdown + JSON) suitable for perf-canary gating and review. The intent is to make selector changes measurable and repeatable across SKUs, and to reduce ad-hoc benchmark scripts during rollout.

Motivation / context: Selector v2 selection is a function of (model family, seq bucket / regime, GPU SKU). We need benchmark coverage that matches those axes and produces a single artifact that (a) is easy to eyeball in review and (b) can be consumed by perf-canary and release signoff. This is the benchmark-lab side of ENG-3929.

What changed (high-level): Add a declarative “matrix” spec that enumerates GPU targets, models, and prompt distributions; add runner wiring that executes each cell for both selectors (v1 and v2), collecting the same metric schema; add an exporter that produces a comparison table keyed by {gpu, model, prompt_set, seq_bucket, selector_version} with deltas; add CI-friendly artifact naming + upload hooks.

Matrix definition: GPUs: [L4, A10, A100-80GB, H100-SXM]. Models: [llama-3.1-8b-instruct (llama-family), mistral-7b-instruct-v0.3 (mistral-family), qwen2.5-7b-instruct (qwen-family)]. Prompt sets: (1) chat_short (median prompt ~250 tokens), (2) chat_medium (~1.5k tokens), (3) rag_long (~8k tokens), (4) long_context_sweep (1k/4k/8k/16k buckets; prefill-heavy). Each prompt set is run with fixed seeds and a warmup phase.

Metrics collected: p50/p95 end-to-end latency, prefill latency, decode latency, tok/s (decode), effective tok/s (prefill+decode), GPU utilization proxy (sm_eff via nvml sampling when available), error rate, NaN/inf flags (if emitted by runtime), and selector telemetry fields as tags (selector_version, kernel_id, model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_normalized).

Exporter output: 1) comparison.csv (one row per cell) 2) comparison.md (human-readable table grouped by GPU then model, with top regressions highlighted) 3) comparison.json (same rows; intended for perf-canary ingestion). The exporter also writes a short “run_summary.md” with runtime version + git SHAs, runner args, and any skipped cells.

How to run locally: ./bench/run_matrix.py --matrix configs/matrices/selector_v2_default.yaml --out /tmp/selector_v2_matrix --selectors v1,v2 --repetitions 5 --warmup 1. For remote lab runs: ./bench/submit_job.py --matrix configs/matrices/selector_v2_default.yaml --selectors v1,v2 --cluster perf-lab-us-east --artifact-prefix gs://redwood-benchmarks/selector-v2/ (see docs in docs/selector_v2_matrix.md).

Implementation details: - New matrix schema: configs/matrices/selector_v2_default.yaml (validated via pydantic) - Runner splits each scenario into explicit prefill + decode windows when the runtime reports them; otherwise falls back to “total latency” only (flagged in output as has_phase_split=false). - Stable ordering for table keys: gpu_sku_normalized, model_id, prompt_set_id, seq_bucket_id, selector_version to minimize diff noise across runs. - Added a small “normalization” layer to map GPU names coming from the lab inventory into the same SKU strings used by selector v2 telemetry (e.g., “NVIDIA A10G” -> “A10”).

Notes / limitations: - The harness does not attempt to infer selector v2’s internal decision path; it relies on runtime-emitted tags (kernel_id, seq_bucket, etc.). If those tags are missing, the cell is marked incomplete and excluded from “top regressions” ranking. - NVML sampling is best-effort and is disabled by default in CI; it’s enabled in the perf lab environment where permissions are available. - We intentionally bucket by seq length rather than logging raw lengths, to keep cardinality aligned with runtime telemetry standards.

Screenshots / sample output: Included in docs/selector_v2_matrix.md a snippet of the generated comparison.md table; example: H100 / qwen2.5-7b-instruct / rag_long shows decode tok/s +6.1% (v2) with p95 total latency -3.4%; A10 / mistral / long_context_sweep initially showed a +8-10% p95 regression in earlier ad-hoc runs; with this harness the regression is reproducible and isolated to seq_bucket=long_prefill (useful for follow-up in runtime).

Testing: - unit: schema validation + deterministic table key ordering - integration (CI): runs a reduced matrix (1 GPU emulator target + 1 model stub + 1 prompt set) to verify end-to-end export without requiring GPUs - lab: manual run in perf-lab-us-east (job link in internal comment)

Rollout / usage: This is intended to be the default artifact for selector v2 rollout signoff and for perf-canary gating thresholds (ENG-3930). Release Eng / SRE can reference the generated comparison.md in go/no-go reviews.

Changelog: Added selector v2 matrix runner + exporter; no changes to existing baseline benchmark suites.

Related: ENG-3929 (benchmark-lab updates), ENG-3921 (project umbrella).
commits: bench(matrix): add selector_v2_default matrix spec + schema validation
bench(runner): execute selectors v1/v2 per scenario with stable keys
bench(metrics): collect phase split metrics and propagate selector tags
bench(export): write comparison.{csv,md,json} with delta columns
docs: add selector v2 matrix usage + artifact format
review_conversation: Claire Dubois: The comparison table is great, but can we ensure we don’t mix prompt-length sweep buckets with seq_bucket ids coming from runtime? I want the output columns to make it obvious which bucketing scheme is used.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated exporter to include both prompt_bucket_id (harness) and seq_bucket_id (runtime). comparison.md groups by prompt_set first and prints seq_bucket_id as a column; also added a note in docs clarifying the source of each field.
Marcus Reed: Please add a reduced-matrix path for CI so we don’t require GPU runners just to validate formatting + artifact generation.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added ci/test_reduced_matrix.sh and a stub runtime metrics collector; CI now runs reduced-matrix-export and validates non-empty comparison.json + stable ordering.
Grace Kim: For selector tags, if kernel_id is missing we should not compute deltas for that row (otherwise people will assume it was “v2”)—can we mark rows incomplete explicitly?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Done. Rows now include completeness=complete|incomplete and incomplete rows are excluded from top_regressions ranking; still emitted for debugging.
Sana Farid: Nit: delta columns should be signed and include units in the markdown header. Also please sort regressions by p95_total_latency first, then tok/s.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated header + sorting logic; markdown now shows “Δ p95_total_ms” and “Δ decode_tok_s” with signed formatting.
release_notes: Benchmark-lab now supports a selector v2 benchmark matrix (GPU/model/prompt) and exports v1 vs v2 comparison artifacts (CSV/MD/JSON) for rollout signoff and perf-canary gating.
